title: I Followed the Badge Override Through Three Buildings After They Fired the Night Guard

parts.text: They fired Luis, the night guard who actually walked the floors, and told us to use an override code the new vendor posted on a sticky in the lobby. I was thirty-six, facilities adjacent, holding a badge that still had Luis's Sharpie smiley on the lanyard clip. At 11:08 p.m. the sticky code opened Building A and also, I noticed, the stairwell to B. The vendor said it was temporary. Temporary codes that open two buildings are not temporary. I photographed the sticky, the doors, the time. Then a man I did not know walked in behind me using the same numbers, waving like we were coworkers. We were not.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: A stranger just used the lobby sticky to follow me toward Building B.

social.video_title: They replaced a guard with a sticky that opened two buildings — Part 1/3
social.description: Night shift, Luis gone, a code on paper. A stranger waved. Would you have let the door close?

parts.text: I let the door close without him and called the after-hours line. They said log it in the morning. I logged it at 11:12 anyway, then walked to Building C because my actual work was a leak in a mechanical room. The same code opened C. Three buildings, one sticky, zero Luis. I shut the mechanical room and sat with the leak like it was a witness. At 11:40 the stranger was in the parking garage trying codes on the gate keypad. The camera there still worked because Luis had insisted. I forwarded the garage still to the morning ticket and cc'd HR safety.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The stranger is on the garage keypad; HR safety now has the still.

social.video_title: The sticky opened C and he tried the garage next — Part 2/3
social.description: Mechanical leak, three doors, a garage camera Luis fought for. Morning was too late. Would you have gone home?

parts.text: Morning turned into a vendor meeting. The sticky came down. Codes rotated. They contracted a walking guard again, not Luis, because companies rarely unfire the person who was right. I kept the smiley clip. The leak got a work order. The stranger was trespassed. HR sent a note about not posting codes. I forwarded my 11:12 ticket as a reply-all without commentary. Commentary was the ticket. Night is a place that needs legs, not paper. I badge in with one building at a time now. That is how buildings stay buildings.

social.video_title: The sticky came down and the walking started again — Part 3/3
social.description: Rotated codes, trespass, a smiley clip. Not Luis, but legs. Was a sticky ever a guard?
